_comment: Project-wide Claude Code permission baseline (checked in) — every session AND background subagent on this repo inherits allow/deny (confirmed: sub-agents inherit the parent's rules). Personal extras go in .claude/settings.local.json (gitignored). Scope: build/test/git/gh, common read-only pipe helpers, pinned Godot + ComfyUI + Ollama local tooling, docs-research web domains. IMPORTANT for agents: NEVER cd-prefix commands (a compound is permission-checked per-subcommand, and `cd <path>` is a Read-path check) — use `git -C <abs>`, `gh --repo`, absolute paths, and the Monitor tool instead of `for`/`sleep` poll loops. deny block below is the hard destructive-op boundary (no rm/del, no non-localhost curl). 2026-08-02: added the automation GLUE an unattended run needs — jq/comm/diff/tee/xargs/basename/dirname/date/stat/touch/mv, true/false, the Windows-path form of the Godot binary (the /c/Tools form did not cover `C:/Tools/...`), and the PowerShell verbs the art/receipt scripts use. Deployment itself (git/gh/dotnet/godot) was already allowed; overnight runs were stalling on the helpers around it, not on the deploy. 2026-08-09 (owner ruling): the blanket rm/del deny WAS relaxed, because it stopped real work — an agent could not delete its own scratch file or a directory of already-ingested screenshots, and the workaround was to leave litter behind and apologise for it. Targeted deletes are now allowed; RECURSIVE deletes stay denied (rm -r / -rf / -fr, Remove-Item -Recurse). Deny outranks allow, so `rm scratch.txt` runs and `rm -rf <dir>` still stops and asks. That is where the danger actually lives: subagents run unattended in worktrees, one bad path variable in a recursive delete is unrecoverable, while a wrong single-file delete is one `git checkout` away. Do not 'simplify' this by deleting the deny block. 2026-09-11 (owner ruling, "go FULL auto, stop asking"): added the whitelist an unattended overnight run on THIS project actually needs. The load-bearing one is Write(//c/Code/**) -- Read and Edit were granted and Write never was, so creating any new file prompted, and a prompt at 3am is a stalled night. That is the same shape the adversarial review found in the source system's own unattended profile, where the deny list blocked the very `gh pr merge` its loop had to issue. Also added: the harness tools the loop's procedure calls by name (Agent/Skill/Monitor/Task*), the PowerShell verbs tools/loop/ci-watch.ps1 and the art scripts use, the launcher and the Godot binary by every path form they are really invoked with, and ordinary shell glue. NOTHING new was installed on the device -- every path here points at a tool that was already present. The recursive-delete deny block below is untouched and stays untouched.
